# Extended Data Table 1. The ten levers and their levels, with values and sources (generated by tools/pathways_methods.py; do not edit; main-paper Table 1 is LEVERS_TABLE_MAIN.md)

**Theoretical Limit = the best value observed, internationally where a comparable measure exists, otherwise in New Zealand, or a documented scenario bound; a logical bound only where physically attainable by choice or design.**

Ambition levels follow the 2050 Pathways Calculator (DECC 2010; DESNZ 2023) and EUCalc (Kockat et al. 2019, Table 2): Reference = Level 1, Moderate = Level 2, Ambitious = Level 3, theoretical limit (TL) = Level 4. One rule for every lever (the 'rule' column): the Reference is current practice held (2023 / 2025 values; business-as-usual technology change applies in every run); Moderate is the midpoint of the Reference and Ambitious (exact for every lever); Ambitious is a documented frontier: a value achieved in New Zealand or elsewhere, an official projection, a peer-reviewed scenario or a documented requirement, and is cited. Theoretical Limit = the best value observed, internationally where a comparable measure exists, otherwise in New Zealand, or a documented scenario bound; a logical bound only where physically attainable by choice or design. Ambitious takes the first applicable sub-rule: A, a case-study distribution exists: the Harrell-Davis q0.15 quantile of the pooled scale-free case ratios (the top-15% convention of the EU Taxonomy, Delegated Regulation 2021/2139, Annex I s. 7.7), with a percentile bootstrap interval; B, an NZ record with no structural trend exists: the best value ever observed in NZ; C, otherwise: a published reference value (official projection > legislated target > peer-reviewed scenario > peer-country value). Moderate is the exact midpoint between the Reference and Ambitious in the lever's native parameter (per year for the path levers L1, L8, L9 and L10). Every lever at TL is asserted at least as strong as Ambitious. Every level moves from the Reference along the normalised logistic 2026 -> 2035 (midpoint 2030.5, k = ln(81)/6), with two documented exceptions: L10 follows the scenario path of its source, which is its timing (m = 1 up to the observed year 2026); L1 at TL rises at the fastest observed inter-census change of household size (the behavioural speed limit) and reaches its level after 2035. Decarbonisation operates on materials (items), aggregated to case studies and typologies by the same pooling; the Ambitious production multiplier is uniform across materials because Horup et al. report the 1.5 °C envelope by archetype only.

1. L3: 40% fewer demolitions, including the recent redevelopment surge (France, 150,000 to 90,000 demolitions a year; Pellan et al. 2024). The surge is the part of net replacement above the long-run rate, i.e. demolition-and-rebuild.
2. L10: the nine background scenarios of Horup et al. (2025, Table S1; integrated assessment model REMIND, Sacchi et al. 2023). SSPs (Shared Socioeconomic Pathways) describe how the world develops (SSP1 sustainable, SSP2 middle of the road, SSP5 fossil-fuelled growth); RCPs (Representative Concentration Pathways) describe climate policy, named by the radiative forcing reached in 2100 in W m⁻² (RCP2.6 ≈ 2 °C, RCP1.9 ≈ 1.5 °C of warming); 'no climate policy' is the baseline. Three SSPs × three climate settings = nine futures for how electricity and industry decarbonise, which set how much cleaner each material becomes.
